memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When the chief baker saw that Joseph had given a favorable interpretation, he said to Joseph, 'I too had a dream: On my head were three baskets of bread. In the top basket were all kinds of baked goods for Pharaoh, but the birds were eating them out of the basket on my head.'" - Gen 40:16-17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chief baker had been listening, and when he sees that the cupbearer received a favorable interpretation, he eagerly tells his own dream, clearly hoping for equally good news. He describes three baskets of bread on his head, with the top one full of baked goods for Pharaoh — but the birds are eating them away.

Notice the baker's motivation: he speaks up only after the good report, hoping his dream will mean the same happy outcome. There is something very human in this. We naturally want good news, and we tend to seek out interpretations, opinions, and messages that tell us what we want to hear. But wanting a favorable answer does not make an answer true.

This is a gentle caution for us. We can be tempted to look only for the encouraging word, to surround ourselves with voices that flatter us, and to avoid anyone who might tell us something hard. But truth is not decided by what we wish to hear. Sometimes the message we need most is not the one we hoped for.

Ask God for the humility to want the truth more than mere comfort. It is better to hear a hard truth that is real than a pleasant word that is false. Seek honest counsel, not just agreeable voices, and let God's Word tell you what is true, whether it is what you wanted or not.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I seek the truth, or only the answer I want to hear?
2. Do I surround myself with honest voices or flattering ones?
3. Am I willing to hear a hard truth over a pleasant falsehood?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, give me the humility to want truth more than comfort. Keep me from seeking only flattering words, and help me to welcome honest counsel and Your truth, even when it is hard. Amen.
